question: A shopkeeper purchased 48 dozens of articles at the rate of ₹300 per dozen. He sold each one of them at the rate of ₹90. What percentage profit did he make?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost price per article = 300 ÷ 12 = 25

Selling price per article = 90

⇒ Profit per article = 90 − 25 = 65

⇒ Profit % = (65 ÷ 25) × 100 = 260%

**∴ Answer = 260%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 48 dozens, CP = 300 per dozen, SP = 90 per article

⇒ Total articles = 48 × 12 = 576

⇒ Total CP = 48 × 300 = 14400

⇒ Total SP = 576 × 90 = 51840

⇒ Profit = 51840 − 14400 = 37440

⇒ Profit % = (37440 ÷ 14400) × 100

⇒ = 2.6 × 100 = 260%

**∴ Final Answer = 260%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Unit Method:** Always convert dozen to single unit to simplify profit/loss quickly.

**Profit % Formula:** Profit % = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100

**Shortcut Insight:** When SP per unit is given, avoid total calculation — compare per unit directly.
